title: Tensor comparison for a specified bounded quotient model
statement: Let T, A and d be the completed coefficient datum of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and let n be a natural number. Let P be a bounded complex of completed-coefficient module sheaves with a degreewise finite-free-retract package. Suppose its localization is isomorphic to the degree-zero quotient sheaf A/I^(n+1), with the completed-ring action specified by the actual quotient projection. Then the localized tensor functor with P of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-tensor-products] is naturally isomorphic to derived scalar extension to that quotient followed by scalar restriction. The complex, bounds, splitting package and realization are all inputs; no resolution-existence assertion is made.

source.place: first proof sentence: compare tensor with a bounded finite-projective quotient representative to finite scalar reduction

proof.text: For every K-flat test complex C, apply the one-K-flat representative comparison of ringedDerived_closed_symmetric_monoidal. Its tensor functor carries the given coefficient isomorphism Q(P) ≅ Q(Z) to an isomorphism between localized total tensor with P and with the degree-zero quotient Z. The recorded representative naturality and functoriality of derived tensor make the comparison natural on the full K-flat homotopy subcategory. The localization factorization of finiteProjectiveTensorRight fixes the first endpoint.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-reduction-ordinary-tensor-comparison], now proved, to identify total tensor with the degree-zero quotient with termwise ordinary scalar extension followed by restriction, naturally on all complexes.

The normalized universal derived extension comparison is invertible on K-flat test complexes, and scalar restriction is exact. Thus the preceding calculation compares with the specified finite reduction functor. K-flat localization extends the natural isomorphism to the whole derived category; the factorization of finiteProjectiveTensorRight identifies the other endpoint.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: ordinary ModuleCat, PresheafOfModules and SheafOfModules restriction of scalars, the ordinary scalar adjunction unit and a scalar pseudofunctor. None provides the derived tensor comparison.

mathlib_searches.query: A specified bounded perfect model of a quotient sheaf induces a natural isomorphism between its localized tensor functor and derived extension followed by restriction of scalars
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: PresheafOfModules.sheafificationCompForgetCompToPresheaf, sheafificationCompToSheaf, ordinary scalar localization, LightCondensed monoidal sheafification, cotangent tensor, a Serre-class localization, Tor and finite-presentation scalar extension. None identifies these unbounded derived sheaf functors.
CategoryTheory.Functor.leftDerivedUnique: uniqueness of universal left-derived functors; useful for the comparison, but does not supply a coefficient model or a Roos comparison.

The specialized functors occur only in AdicCoefficientDatumCompleted and FiniteProjectiveTensorProducts. ChangeOfRingsTensorCancellation gives the ordinary natural tensor identity, and SiteDerivedTensorDescentIndependentCoefficients gives the localization interface. No theorem identifies the specialized derived functors for a supplied quotient model.

theorem completedReductionTensorModelComparison (n : ℕ)
    (P : CochainComplex (adicDatumModules T d) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ j : ℤ, j < a ∨ b < j → IsZero (P.X j))
    (p : SheafOfModules.StrictPerfectCoefficientPackageOnSite
      ((adicLisseForget T).obj (adicDatumRing T d)) P)
    (e : (completedConstantQ _).obj P ≅
      (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (adicDatumModules T d) 0).obj
        (CompletedConstantReduction.residue T d.ideal n)) :
    Nonempty (finiteProjectiveTensorRight T d P hb p ≅
      adicDatumReductionUnderlying T d n)
